13.
Notwithstanding anything contained in any law for
the time being in force–

(a)
no court shall impose a sentence under this Act for
a contempt of court unless it is  satisfied that the
contempt  is  of  such  a  nature  that  it  substantially
interferes,  or  tends  substantially  to  interfere  with
the due course of justice;

(b)
the  court  may  permit,  in  any  proceeding  for
contempt of court, justification by truth as a valid
defense if it is satisfied that it is in public interest
and  the  request  for  invoking  the  said  defense  is
bonafide.

14.
